source_text.body:
Clear daily game tasks in Honkai: Star Rail by computer use
NUS researchers had Claude Computer Use open menus, pick a stage, set run counts and start auto-battle in Honkai: Star Rail, and it also managed decks in Hearthstone.
·
Nov 12, 2026
Done with
CU
Claude computer use
What they did
The NUS team built an automated GUI framework on the Claude Computer Use API. Claude works from live screenshots and keeps the earlier ones as context. Told to finish the day's Simulated Universe, it opened the game menu, found the Golden Calyx, set 6 challenge runs, started auto-battle, waited for the fight to end and exited. Human reviewers monitored the runs.
How it went
It completed the Star Rail routine and also made and renamed Hearthstone decks. Across 20 tasks on 12 apps or sites, it failed on some fine-grained web steps and on Word and PowerPoint text-field selection.
Worth knowing
Tests ran on Windows at 1366x768 and macOS at 1344,756, with human review. Complex interfaces are where it failed.
Try it yourself
with
Claude computer use
Copy prompt
Open [game name] and complete my daily tasks: [list tasks, e.g. spend stamina on stage X, set run count to Y, start auto-battle]. Describe each screen as you go, and stop when all tasks are done or if you hit anything unexpected. Pause and ask me before spending any in-game currency or making any purchase.
Original source: https://www.qbitai.com/2024/12/223558.html
